newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse closes for Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse closes for Christmas.

text.p: The Brussels Bel-20 leading share index closed down on Tuesday after a half-day of trade seen by dealers as very thin. They expected the index to remain quiet until the New Year.
"Today we were in a coma," said one trader.
The Bel-20 share index ended down 0.21 percent or 3.96 points at 1,878.38, with a 843 million francs worth of Belgian shares changing hands.
The index closed at 1230 GMT because of the Christmas holidays. It reopens as normal on Friday December 27.

Retailer Delhaize saw an active volume of 80,399 shares traded after one major investor dumped his Delhaize stocks, but the share managed to regain ground minutes before closing to end up 1.35 percent at 1,880 francs.

Dealers said the libel case victory by U.S. Food Lion, a unit of Delhaize, against ABC television was seen as "good news". But they added that it was not likely to lead to the 1.7 billion francs compensation demanded by Food Lion.
Societe Generale de Belgique lost 1.31 percent to close at 11,325 francs, with one dealer putting it down to end of year profittaking.
Elsewhere attention was on steel maker Cockerill Sambre which closed unchanged at 114 francs but saw a strong volume of its shares traded as the market readjusted to its recent Bel-20 departure.
"Cockerill's movements was an adjustment to leaving the index," said a trader.
